description: The physics and engineering of mobile radio: from the generations of cellular standards through channel models, cellular design, digital modulation and coding in fading channels, multiple antennas and OFDM, and multiple access, with every link simulated and its error rate measured. Taught to the depth of a leading wireless communications course.
modelledOn: Rappaport, Wireless Communications: Principles and Practice
Tse and Viswanath, Fundamentals of Wireless Communication
outcomes: Trace the evolution from 1G to 5G and explain the architecture and key technologies of each generation.
Model path loss, shadowing and multipath fading and classify channels as narrowband or wideband, slow or fast.
Design a cellular layout with frequency reuse and compute signal-to-interference ratio, capacity and trunking performance.
Derive error probabilities for digital modulation in AWGN and fading channels and simulate them.
Explain channel coding, diversity, MIMO and OFDM and quantify their gains.
Compare TDMA, FDMA, CDMA and OFDMA and simulate a complete wireless link in MATLAB or Python.

units.title: Wireless communication systems and standards
topics: History: from Marconi to 5G; 1G AMPS, 2G GSM and IS-95, 2.5G GPRS/EDGE, 3G UMTS/CDMA2000, 4G LTE, 5G NR and what 6G research targets
Cellular network architecture: mobiles, base stations, core network, handover, roaming, SIM and authentication
Spectrum: allocation, licensing, Ghana's NCA bands, unlicensed bands (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, LoRa)
Other wireless systems: satellite, WLAN, WPAN, microwave links; coverage in rural Ghana
Simulation environment: MATLAB or Python with NumPy and SciPy

units.title: Modulation schemes and the radio link
topics: Analog modulation review: AM, FM; the transmitter and receiver chain; mixers, filters, amplifiers
Digital modulation overview: ASK, FSK, PSK, QAM; bandwidth efficiency and power efficiency
Pulse shaping, intersymbol interference, raised-cosine filters, eye diagrams
Link budget: transmit power, antenna gain, path loss, noise figure, receiver sensitivity

units.title: Statistical channel models: narrowband and wideband fading
topics: Large-scale propagation: free space, two-ray, log-distance path loss, empirical models (Okumura-Hata, COST 231); log-normal shadowing
Small-scale multipath: delay spread, coherence bandwidth, Doppler spread, coherence time
Narrowband fading: Rayleigh and Rician distributions; level crossing rate and fade duration
Wideband channels: tapped delay line models, power delay profile, frequency-selective fading
Classifying channels: flat versus frequency selective, slow versus fast; simulating Rayleigh fading (Jakes model)

units.title: Cellular concepts and system design
topics: The cellular concept: cells, clusters, frequency reuse, reuse distance and the cluster size
Co-channel and adjacent-channel interference; signal-to-interference ratio versus cluster size
Capacity: channels per cell, spectral efficiency; improving capacity with sectoring, cell splitting, microcells
Handover strategies, power control, mobility management
Designing a cellular layout for a Ghanaian town with given traffic and coverage targets

units.title: Quality of service and trunking
topics: Traffic theory: Erlangs, offered load, grade of service
Erlang B and Erlang C formulas; blocked-calls-cleared versus queued systems; trunking efficiency
QoS parameters for voice, data and video; delay, jitter, loss; scheduling in LTE
Dimensioning a cell's channels for a target blocking probability

units.title: Digital modulation and detection in AWGN; error probabilities
topics: Signal space representation; matched filter and correlation receivers; maximum likelihood detection
Error probabilities in AWGN for BPSK, QPSK, M-PSK, M-QAM, FSK; the Q-function and union bound
Performance in fading: average BER in Rayleigh fading and the diversity order; outage probability
Synchronisation and channel estimation in brief
Monte Carlo BER simulation and comparison with theory

units.title: Coding for wireless channels
topics: Channel capacity (Shannon) for AWGN and fading channels; coding gain
Block codes (Hamming, Reed-Solomon), convolutional codes and Viterbi decoding; interleaving against bursts
Turbo codes, LDPC and polar codes as used in 3G, 4G and 5G
Hybrid ARQ and adaptive modulation and coding

units.title: Multiple antenna systems: diversity, MIMO, OFDM
topics: Diversity: time, frequency, space; selection, equal-gain and maximal-ratio combining
MIMO: spatial multiplexing, capacity scaling, space-time codes (Alamouti), beamforming, massive MIMO in 5G
OFDM: orthogonal subcarriers, IFFT/FFT implementation, cyclic prefix, PAPR; OFDM in Wi-Fi, LTE and 5G
Simulating an OFDM link over a frequency-selective channel

units.title: Multiple access: TDMA, FDMA, CDMA and beyond
topics: FDMA, TDMA and their use in 1G and GSM; frame structures
CDMA: spreading codes, processing gain, near-far problem and power control, RAKE receiver; IS-95 and UMTS
OFDMA and SC-FDMA in LTE; NOMA and random access (ALOHA, CSMA) for Wi-Fi and IoT
Capacity comparison of multiple access schemes
Capstone: a MATLAB-style end-to-end simulation of a cellular link with fading, coding, modulation and multiple access
